title: India Has Never Played at a World Cup. This Month, Four Players with Indian Roots Will.
excerpt: A Punjabi from Auckland, a Keralite from Doha, a Tamil-Australian from Melbourne, and an Indo-Caribbean midfielder from France — all at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
body:
India has never played at a FIFA World Cup. The Blue Tigers' qualification dreams were crushed again in the second round of the 2026 qualifiers, and for the 1.4 billion people who call the subcontinent home, the wait continues.

But when the biggest football tournament in history kicks off across the United States, Canada, and Mexico on June 11, four players with Indian roots will be there. For the first time ever, four footballers of Indian descent will feature at a World Cup, representing four different countries across four different continents.

## Sarpreet Singh — New Zealand

The most recognisable name on this list is Sarpreet Singh, a 27-year-old attacking midfielder whose parents emigrated from Jalandhar, Punjab, to Auckland before he was born.

Singh made history in 2019 when he became the first footballer of Indian descent to play in Germany's Bundesliga, making his debut for Bayern Munich. He was part of Bayern's title-winning squad in the 2019-20 season under Hansi Flick — the same season the club won the Champions League.

"I'm from a very typical Punjabi family with a lot of uncles and aunties and cousins," Singh told *Sportstar*. "We always used to play backyard cricket, a bit of basketball."

Currently on loan at Wellington Phoenix from Serbian club TSC Bačka Topola, Singh has earned 24 caps for New Zealand and will wear the number 10 shirt when the All Whites open their World Cup campaign against Iran in Los Angeles on June 16.

Indian fans may remember him from the 2018 Intercontinental Cup in Mumbai, where he registered two assists in New Zealand's 2-1 victory over India. "That was a crazy experience," he recalled. "It's a little bit strange being a Singh and playing for New Zealand in India against India."

## Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid — Qatar

Perhaps the most emotionally resonant story for the Indian diaspora belongs to 19-year-old Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid, whose parents hail from Kannur district in Kerala. His father Jamshid is from Thalassery; his mother Shyma is from Valapattanam.

Born and raised in Doha, Tahsin developed through Qatar's Aspire Academy — one of Asia's most prestigious football development centres — and currently plays for Al Duhail SC in the Qatar Stars League. He became the first player of Indian origin to feature in the league.

"This is such a joyous moment for me personally. To see my son achieve the heights I dreamt of at his age is truly remarkable," his father told *The Times of India* from Doha.

Senior Congress MP Shashi Tharoor hailed the selection, noting Tahsin is "the first player of Indian origin to be selected for the Qatar national football team." If he takes the field, Tahsin will become the first footballer with Indian roots to actually play in a FIFA World Cup match — beating Sarpreet Singh to a distinction both could claim.

## Nishan Velupillay — Australia

Melbourne-born Nishan Velupillay, 25, has an Anglo-Indian mother and a Malaysian father of Sri Lankan Tamil descent. The winger plays for Melbourne Victory and broke into the Socceroos squad after a standout A-League season under coach Tony Popovic.

His international debut was memorable: he scored against China during the World Cup qualifiers, instantly announcing himself as a dangerous attacking option. Australia have been drawn in a challenging group, but Velupillay's pace and directness could earn him meaningful minutes.

## Samuel Moutoussamy — DR Congo

The most distant connection to India, but a genuine one: Samuel Moutoussamy, 29, plays for Greek club Atromitos and represents DR Congo. His father is an Indo-Guadeloupean of Tamil origin — part of the community that traces its ancestry to Indian labourers who migrated to the Caribbean during the late nineteenth century. His mother is Congolese.

Moutoussamy has earned more than 50 caps for DR Congo and is an established figure in their midfield. Previously with French club Nantes and Turkish side Sivasspor, he brings both European tactical nous and international experience to a DR Congo side making their first World Cup appearance since 1974 (when they were known as Zaire).

## What This Means for Indian Football Fans

The 2026 World Cup runs from June 11 to July 19 across 16 host cities. For the first time, 48 teams will compete — up from 32 — meaning 104 matches across six weeks. Zee Entertainment has secured the broadcast rights in India through its new Unite8 Sports channels, with streaming available on ZEE5.

For NRIs across the United States and Canada, many matches will be played in local time zones — and with four players carrying Indian DNA on the pitch, this World Cup may feel closer to home than any before it. They follow in the footsteps of Vikash Dhorasoo, whose Andhra Pradesh roots carried him to the 2006 World Cup with France. Two decades later, the diaspora's football footprint has quadrupled.

*Sources: IndiaSportsHub, Livemint, Sporting News, JagranJosh, Times of India*
